messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: prod us-west-2 ELB error-rate spike (>= 8:12 UTC). 3xx/5xx + latency. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/networking-elb. Auto page to oncall maya.@here

maya (oncall): Got the page. Checking dashboard now. 504s concentrated in us-west-2a targetgroup tg-0a1b2c.

lee: I'm seeing target health flapping for tg-0a1b2c in CloudWatch - healthy count dropping from 48 -> 30 in 3m. CPU on some targets is fine but ELB backend_conn_fail increased.

maya (oncall): Any EBS/IO errors? Could be underlying instances hitting EBS throttling.

sanjay: I'll run `describe-instances` and check CloudWatch EBS metrics for those instance IDs. Running: `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=instance-id,Values=i-0abcde1,i-0abcde2`

infra-bot: Log marker added: INCIDENT-5812345678. Snapshotting ELB access logs to s3://redwood-incidents/5812345678/ for postmortem.

olivia: I'm on customer impact triage. Preliminary: ~12-18% of external requests hitting us-west-2 see 5xx/504; embeddings/streaming endpoints show higher latency/timeouts. Some Dedicated customers on reserved capacity reported errors in the last 10m. No full account outages reported yet.

lee: I pulled metrics from the target instances. EBS read_iops spiked on i-0abcde1 and i-0fghij3; dmesg shows `ext4: delayed allocation failed` and repeated NRQ timeouts. Suspect degraded volumes on a subset of hosts.

maya (oncall): OK. Mitigation plan: 1) Drain affected targets from targetgroup, 2) Shift Route53 weight away from us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 (warm region) at 70% immediately, 3) Open AWS case for EBS degraded storage and request expedited EBS repair. If failover needed, increase to 90%.

sanjay: Deregistering the flapping targets now: ```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c/abcdef --targets Id=i-0abcde1 Id=i-0fghij3
```

lee: Confirmed deregister call returned 200. ELB health now shows draining for those instances. Draining should reduce immediate 5xx.

olivia: Notifying CS: "We're experiencing partial regional degradation in us-west-2 affecting some requests. We're shifting traffic and replacing affected hosts. No data loss expected." Sending to cs-team channel. :loudspeaker:

incident-bot: ACTION: Created AWS Support case #1234567890. TAM notified. Case link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=1234567890

aws-tam-bot: TAM assigned: Priya K. Investigating underlying EBS performance event in us-west-2a. Reported correlated EC2 host-level IO errors.

maya (oncall): Executing Route53 weight shift. Using change-batch to move 70% to eu-west-1 for the api record: ```json
{"Comment":"Shift traffic for INCIDENT-5812345678","Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.prod.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":700,"Region":"eu-west-1","TTL":60}},{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.prod.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2","Weight":300,"Region":"us-west-2","TTL":60}}]}
```

infra-bot: Route53 change submitted: change ID /change/CMPLX123. Propagation to edge ~1-2m. Monitor global synthetic probes.

lee: After drain, 5xxs in us-west-2 dropped from 12% -> 4% over 4m. Latency for streaming still elevated for some sessions (~600ms -> 1s). Streams may need reconnect fallback.

olivia: CS update posted. A handful of enterprise customers opened support tickets referencing higher latency — triage updated docs with recommended reconnect guidance for streaming clients.

maya (oncall): Auto-scaling to replace affected hosts. Kicking off instance replacement: `aws autoscaling set-instance-health --instance-id i-0abcde1 --health-status Unhealthy --auto-scaling-group-name asg-frontend-prod`

lee: New instances launching and registering. New targets healthy in about ~90s. Monitoring for residual errors.

sanjay: AWS response: EBS reported degraded performance on gp3 volumes in us-west-2a due to underlying host EBS network congestion. They're performing host remediation and live-moving volumes. They recommend replacing affected EC2 hosts and reattaching volumes as necessary.

maya (oncall): Good. We're continuing with instance replacements. No database or persistent storage corruption noted. Critical: ensure we don't attach affected volumes to other hosts until AWS confirms stable.

olivia: Customer impact summary for now (internal): "Partial regional degradation in us-west-2a; ~12% of requests briefly affected, mitigated by draining targets and shifting 70% traffic to eu-west-1. Some streaming sessions experienced reconnects. No persistent data loss. CS escalations opened for 3 enterprise customers."

incident-bot: Notify: If unresolved in 30 minutes escalate to L3 and manager oncall. Timer started.

lee: Noticed one edge cache node in us-west-2 still showing elevated 502s. Flushing its nginx upstreams helped temporarily. Command used: `sudo systemctl restart nginx` on edge-uw2a-01. We'll replace the host via ASG too.

aws-tam-bot: AWS ETA for full host remediation ~45-60m per TAM. They recommend leaving Route53 weight shift in place until we confirm stable IO.

maya (oncall): Agree. Keep route53 weights at 70/30 until further notice. Continue replacing unhealthy hosts. Olivia, keep CS updates every 15m. Lee/Sanjay — coordinate to keep me posted on new node registrations and any lingering 5xx.

olivia: Posted customer-facing status update: "Partial regional degradation in us-west-2, we've shifted traffic and are actively remediating. Next update in 15m." Sent to status page.

lee: New instances are healthy and serving traffic. us-west-2 5xx rate now down to ~1.1%. Latency within SLO for most endpoints.

maya (oncall): Good. Cancel escalation timer. Incident remains in mitigation -> recovery. Handing off to lee for next 30m watch and postmortem notes. I'll remain available if AWS asks for anything.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: maya -> lee. Handoff metadata: start=5812345900, duration=1800s.

lee: Taking watch. I'll capture timeline and initial action items for postmortem. Key items: (1) Confirmed EBS network host congestion in us-west-2a, (2) drained/flushed affected targets, (3) shifted Route53 weights, (4) replaced unhealthy hosts.

olivia: Final customer note drafted for postmortem: "Cause: degraded EBS performance affecting a subset of instances in us-west-2a, resulting in increased 5xx and latency. Mitigation: drained affected targets, shifted traffic to eu-west-1, replaced instances, and coordinated with AWS TAM for host remediation. Impact: transient errors for ~12-18% of traffic; no data loss. Next steps: postmortem and long-term mitigations (traffic steering playbook update, runbook EBS detection thresholds)."

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated -> monitoring. Close when postmortem created.
